# Introduction

The 1999 Polish administrative reform consolidated 49 voivodeships into 16, stripping
31 cities of their regional capital status while retaining 18 (including two dual-capital
arrangements). This paper exploits that discontinuous, simultaneous redesignation as a
natural experiment to estimate the causal effect of administrative capital-status loss on
local economic trajectories.

The primary research question is: **Did losing voivodeship-capital status in 1999
causally reduce population growth, firm density, and labour market outcomes in
affected Polish cities over the subsequent two decades?**

We employ a two-way fixed-effects (TWFE) difference-in-differences estimator with
event-study leads and lags, supplemented by propensity-score-matched DiD and synthetic
control analyses for selected large demoted cities. Data come from the Polish Local
Data Bank (GUS BDL) at the powiat level and Eurostat REGIO at NUTS-3 for GDP.

# Data and Measurement

## Treatment assignment

Treatment is defined at the city-powiat (powiat grodzki) level. The 31 demoted cities
constitute the treatment group; the 18 retained capitals form the primary control group.
Two dual-capital pairs (Bydgoszcz/Toruń; Gorzów Wielkopolski/Zielona Góra) retain
capital functions and are coded as control units, with sensitivity checks excluding them.

## Outcome variables

```{r outcomes-table}
outcomes_df <- tibble::tribble(

  "REGON firms per 1,000 pop.", "GUS BDL", "Powiat", "Annual", "1995–2023",
  "Log avg. gross wage (PLN)", "GUS BDL", "Powiat", "Annual", "2002–2023",
  "Log GDP per capita (EUR)", "Eurostat REGIO nama_10r_3gdp", "NUTS-3", "Annual", "2000–2022"
)
kable(outcomes_df, booktabs = TRUE,

```

# Identification Strategy

## Parallel trends assumption

The DiD estimator is consistent if, absent the 1999 reform, demoted and retained cities
would have followed parallel trends. This is assessed visually via group-mean trend plots
(Figure \@ref(fig:pretrends)) and formally tested using pre-reform event-study coefficients
(β_{k<0} ≈ 0).

**Threats to identification:**

1. *Selection into demotion*: If the reform targeted already-declining cities, pre-trends
   may diverge, biasing DiD estimates downward. Addressed by PSM on 1998 baseline
   characteristics and pre-trend testing.
2. *SUTVA / spatial spillovers*: Retained capitals may absorb displaced workers/firms from
   nearby demoted cities, violating the stable-unit-treatment-value assumption. Tested by
   excluding demoted cities in the same voivodeship as their retained capital.
3. *Post-1999 shocks*: EU accession (2004) and structural fund inflows differentially
   affected regions. Included via region × year fixed effects in extended specifications.

## Specification

The primary event-study specification is:

$$Y_{it} = \alpha_i + \lambda_t + \sum_{k \neq -1} \beta_k \left(D_i \times \mathbf{1}[t - 1999 = k]\right) + \varepsilon_{it}$$

where $\alpha_i$ are powiat fixed effects, $\lambda_t$ are year fixed effects, $D_i = 1$
for demoted cities, and $k = -1$ (year 1998) is the omitted reference period.
Standard errors are clustered at the powiat level.

The ATT from the two-term DiD ($D_i \times Post_t$) is reported as the primary scalar
estimate; the event-study plot reveals dynamic effects.

# Results

## Pre-trend test

```{r pretrends, fig.cap="Group-mean trends: demoted vs. retained capitals. Vertical dashed line = 1999 reform. Flat pre-period trends support parallel-trends assumption.", out.width="95%"}
knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "f01_group_trends.png"))
```

## Balance table

```{r balance}
bal_path <- here("figures", "t01_balance_table.csv")
if (file.exists(bal_path)) {
  bal <- read_csv(bal_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
  kable(bal, booktabs = TRUE, digits = 3,
        caption = "Pre-reform covariate balance (pre-1999 period means).
                   Norm. diff. > 0.25 indicates potential confounding.") |>
    kable_styling(latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position"), font_size = 9)
} else {
  cat("Balance table not yet generated. Run scripts/04\\_eda.py.")
}
```

## Event-study estimates

```{r es-population, fig.cap="Event-study: effect of capital-status loss on log population. β coefficients relative to 1998 baseline; 95% CI shown. Pre-period β ≈ 0 supports identification.", out.width="90%"}
knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "f04_eventstudy_ln_population.png"))
```

```{r es-firms, fig.cap="Event-study: effect on REGON firms per 1,000 population.", out.width="90%"}

```

## Policy translation

```{r policy-table}
pol_path <- here("figures", "t05_policy_translation.csv")
if (file.exists(pol_path)) {
  pol <- read_csv(pol_path, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    select(outcome, horizon_years, policy_magnitude, beta, ci_lo_95, ci_hi_95)
  kable(pol, booktabs = TRUE, digits = 3,
        caption = "Long-run ATT estimates translated to policy magnitudes.
                   Horizons: 5, 10, 15, 20 years post-reform.") |>
    kable_styling(latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position"), font_size = 9)
} else {
  cat("Policy translation table not yet generated. Run scripts/07\\_translate.py.")
}
```

```{r heterogeneity, fig.cap="Scatter of pre-reform city size vs. post-reform cumulative population change (1998–2019). Tests H2: larger demoted cities show smaller negative effects.", out.width="85%"}

```

# Robustness

```{r robustness}
rob_path <- here("figures", "t04_robustness_summary.csv")

} else {
  cat("Robustness table not yet generated. Run scripts/06\\_robustness.py.")
}
```

# Appendix {-}

## Appendix A: TERYT code verification

All powiat TERYT codes used in this analysis were verified against the GUS TERYT register
(eteryt.stat.gov.pl). Codes in `data/raw/treatment/capital_status_1999.csv` marked
`verify_teryt` were cross-checked before merging. Notable issues: Wałbrzych (TERYT 0265)
lost city-powiat status 2013–2019 and is excluded from the main specification.

## Appendix B: NUTS-3 boundary harmonisation

Eurostat NUTS-3 boundaries for Poland changed in 2004, 2008, and 2015.
The 2021 NUTS-3 classification is used as the reference. Correspondence tables
(Eurostat NUTS 2016 → 2021) were applied to harmonise the GDP series.

## Appendix C: Data availability

All raw data files are static downloads committed under `data/raw/`.
No live API calls were made. Pipeline reproduces fully from raw files via
`scripts/01_ingest.py` through `scripts/07_translate.py`.
